title: Break the quota?

predict.q: B keeps to its quota of 20. A raises its output step by step, from 20 all the way to 40. What happens to A's profit?

options.s: It keeps rising, because A sells more at every step.
options.fb: More output is not always more profit. Each extra unit lowers the price on every unit A sells: past 30 units A's profit falls (875 at 35, 800 at 40).

options.s: It falls from the first step, because the price falls.
options.fb: At first the extra sales outweigh the lower price: 25 × 35 = 875 > 800. A's profit falls only after 30 units.

options.s: It rises at first, then falls back.
options.fb: A's profit goes 800 → 875 → 900 → 875 → 800, while joint profit falls at every step.

options.s: It stays the same, because joint profit is fixed.
options.fb: Joint profit is not fixed: it is highest at the cartel output of 40 (1,600) and falls at every step, to 1,200. B's profit falls at every step too.

task: Move firm A's output slider from 20 to 40 and watch price, each firm's profit and joint profit.

target.do: Move firm A's output slider all the way to 40, then press Check.

takeaway: Cheating pays the cheater (up to a point) but lowers joint profit and the other member's profit.
